title: The Hidden Costs of Not Tracking Your Spending

faq.q: Why is tracking expenses important if I'm already saving?
faq.a: Even if you're saving, tracking helps you understand if your spending aligns with your values and long-term goals. It can reveal opportunities to save more efficiently or redirect funds to higher-priority areas.

faq.q: What's the difference between essential and discretionary expenses?
faq.a: Essential expenses are necessary for living (rent, groceries, utilities). Discretionary expenses are non-essential choices that enhance your lifestyle (dining out, entertainment, travel). Tracking helps distinguish between the two.

faq.q: Can I use a simple notebook to track expenses?
faq.a: Absolutely. A notebook is a perfectly valid and effective method. The key is consistency in recording every transaction, which builds awareness and discipline.

faq.q: How often should I review my expenses?
faq.a: Ideally, review new transactions daily or every few days to ensure accuracy. A more thorough weekly or monthly review helps you analyse trends and make adjustments to your budget.

faq.q: Will tracking expenses restrict my lifestyle?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Tracking isn't about deprivation; it's about awareness and intentionality. It empowers you to make informed choices, potentially cutting back on low-value spending to free up funds for things you truly value, like travel or investments.

faq.q: What if I find my spending is too high?
faq.a: Discovering high spending is the first step to change. Use this insight to create a realistic budget, identify areas where you can cut back, and reallocate those funds towards your savings or investment goals.

based_on.title: Bengaluru couple spends ₹9 lakh yearly on travel as biggest household expense, ₹60,000 on rent: ‘We’re not tracking…’
